papers.title: Flavor Entanglement as a CPT Violation Witness in Neutrino Oscillations
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study linking the single-particle flavor entanglement of a \(ν_{e} \rightarrow ν_μ\) oscillation to CPT violation using the concurrence. In a two-flavor vacuum with CP-conserving mixing, CPT invariance strictly demands \(\mathcal{C}_ν(L) = \mathcal{C}_{\barν}(L)\), meaning any measured difference \(Δ\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{CPT}} \equiv \mathcal{C}_ν - \mathcal{C}_{\barν}\) serves as a clean, background-free witness of CPT violation. We derive exact, first-order analytical relations connecting this entanglement asymmetry to the standard probability asymmetry, the baseline reflection sums, and the long-baseline decoherence floor. To rigorously test the experimental viability of this framework, we perform extensive numerical simulations. We demonstrate that the framework projects stringent sensitivity limits on Standard-Model Extension (SME) parameters at DUNE-like densities, isolate a coordinate-independent CPT invariant, and show that the signal remains robust across realistic, variable Earth matter density profiles. Crucially, we identify a distinct 24-hour sidereal modulation of the entanglement asymmetry, providing a definitive temporal "smoking gun" to disentangle CPT violation from matter effects. Finally, we show that at PeV astrophysical energies, the reflection-sum mismatch scales up to \(10^{13}\) meters, opening a novel frontier for CPT tests beyond terrestrial experiments.

papers.title: The low-luminosity state of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205
papers.abstract: Context. At low accretion rates, X-ray pulsars can develop a two-hump spectrum through the thermalization and Comptonization of cyclotron photons in an accretion-heated, strongly magnetized atmosphere. Sources with independently measured cyclotron-line energies, $E_{\rm cyc}$, are particularly important because they provide a direct estimate of magnetic field strength and allow the continuum shape to be tested against spectral formation models. Aims. We investigate the luminosity-dependent spectral evolution of the Be/X-ray pulsar IGR J06074+2205 and constrain the accretion regime in its newly observed low-luminosity state. Methods. We analyzed three NuSTAR observations obtained during the 2023 and 2025 outbursts, corresponding to the high-, intermediate-, and low-luminosity states at $L_{3-79}\simeq5\times10^{36}$, $4\times10^{35}$, and $6\times10^{34}$ erg s$^{-1}$, respectively. We supplemented these data with Swift/XRT observations and performed broadband spectral analysis of all three states. Results. The high-luminosity spectrum follows a classical cutoff power law, whereas the intermediate- and low-luminosity spectra require two thermal Comptonization components to reproduce their two-hump shape. In the intermediate state, the cyclotron line, first reported at $\sim50$ keV in the high-luminosity state, lies on top of the high-energy hump. We interpret the low-luminosity state as representing stable accretion from a cold disk. IGR J06074+2205 thus joins the very limited sample of X-ray pulsars with cyclotron-line energies that have been observed with a double-humped spectral shape.

papers.title: Geometric optics for gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity: amplitude birefringence and tensor-scalar mixing on general backgrounds
papers.abstract: We study the propagation of high-frequency gravitational waves in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity within the geometric optics approximation. In contrast to previous work, we allow for a general background with a nonvanishing scalar field, which enables a covariant treatment of amplitude birefringence. The background scalar gradient introduces third-derivative terms into the linearized field equations. These must be treated as subleading for the linearized system to be free of ghosts, which yields a covariant upper bound on the frequency. Tensor-scalar mixing is induced by the Weyl curvature through the Newman-Penrose scalar $Ψ_0$ along the ray. When the mixing is efficient, the propagation eigenmodes consist of one luminal, one subluminal, and one superluminal mode, and a violation of the ghost-free condition leads to a classical instability. From the transport equations at next-to-leading order, we show that, when the mixing is negligible, the relative amplitude of the two helicities depends only on the scalar-field gradients along the ray at the emission and observation events, independently of the path in between.

papers.title: Shadows and Images of Black Holes with Purely Nonlinear Scalarization
papers.abstract: We investigate the shadows and radiative images of static, spherically symmetric black holes with purely nonlinear scalarization in Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The quartic exponential coupling supports scalarized backgrounds without a linear tachyonic instability of Schwarzschild black holes. We compare mass and coupling dependences and construct images on radially stable backgrounds using optically thin spherical emission and face-on thin disks. On the sampled radially stable branches, we find smaller shadow radii than those of Schwarzschild black holes at the same mass, with reductions reaching approximately $21.7\%$. The sampled radially unstable branches show much smaller shadow-size deviations. The photon-orbit index, which measures radial instability per unit orbital angle, varies nonmonotonically even when the normalized shadow radius changes monotonically. The index also controls the asymptotic compression of higher-order images, providing information complementary to shadow size. For spherical emission, radial infall produces a darker center relative to the bright ring than static emission. For circular disks, we find that smooth metric variations can create an unstable interval separating two stable regions of timelike circular motion. When the disk occupies the stable region connected to infinity, its inner edge moves outward across this transition, suppressing emission inside the geometric shadow boundary while the normalized shadow radius changes only slightly. Our results show that purely nonlinear scalarization can alter images through both photon propagation and the orbital structure of emitting matter, with the visible features depending on the emission model.

papers.abstract: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces. Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored. Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others. papers.title: Beyond the point lens: radial structure and the horizon in wave-optics gravitational lensing
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave lensing in the wave-optics regime is sensitive to the structure of the lens beyond its total mass: to its exterior radial profile and, as we show, to the boundary condition at its centre. We develop an analytic framework to compute these effects for a scalar wave, as corrections to the wave lensed by a Newtonian point mass. The corrections are organized in inverse powers of the distance from the lens and computed with dressed radial kernels, which include the Newtonian interaction to all orders and resum the long-range phase that invalidates the Born expansion around the free wave. Retaining wavefront curvature, we find that the scattered wave is not the whole response: an inverse-square deformation changes the direct wave by an equal amount, even when the scattered wave is faint. Steeper terms of the exterior potential lead to short-distance divergences, which signal that the exterior geometry alone does not determine the lensed wave: the missing information is a set of local terms fixed by the inner boundary condition. For a Schwarzschild black hole we determine them by matching to the ingoing solution at the horizon. The horizon enters the amplification factor as an absorptive contact term, which reproduces the horizon-area cross section; it is absent for a non-absorbing lens of the same mass, and cannot be described by the thin-lens diffraction integral. It completes the correction quadratic in the mass, where it appears at the same order as finite-distance optical corrections, and largely cancels against them for an aligned source. Together, these results connect Newtonian dressing, diffraction and inner boundary conditions, in a systematic description of corrections to point-mass gravitational-wave lensing.

papers.title: Instantaneous Spectral Bandwidth of Solar Type III Radio Bursts in the Interplanetary Medium
papers.abstract: Magnetic reconnection during solar flares accelerates electron beams that generate type III radio bursts through the plasma emission process. Their instantaneous spectral bandwidth is commonly interpreted as a measure of the spatial extent of the emitting population, yet contributions from viewing angle and radio-wave propagation remain poorly constrained. We investigate bandwidths of 20 type III bursts observed by Parker Solar Probe between 0.15-6.5 MHz. The bandwidth increases with frequency and is consistent with previous measurements up to 100 MHz. For the first time, simultaneous observations from multiple spacecraft show similar bandwidths despite large differences in viewing geometry. We further examine bandwidth contributions from intrinsic emission and propagation effects using numerical and analytical simulations, showing that the beam spatial extent is larger than required to explain observed bandwidths, while the spatial extent of Langmuir wave generation produces electromagnetic emission bandwidths near the observed lower limit. Temporal broadening due to radio-wave scattering can increase the bandwidth by causing emission from different frequencies to overlap in time. This effect depends strongly on turbulence level and becomes increasingly important for faster electron beams and narrower intrinsic emission profiles. The results demonstrate that observed type III bandwidths cannot be interpreted solely in terms of physically emitting regions: the intrinsic emission bandwidth follows the spatial extent of Langmuir wave generation, while propagation-induced temporal broadening provides an additional contribution that can reconcile intrinsic and observed bandwidths. Accounting for radio-wave propagation effects is essential when using type III burst bandwidths to infer the spatial properties of their emitting electron populations.

papers.title: $B\to K a$ decays in QCD factorization and revised bounds on ALP couplings
papers.abstract: Rare flavor-changing processes such as $B\to K a$ offer sensitive probes of axion-like particles (ALPs) for masses below a few GeV. We study this process in the framework of QCD factorization and ALP effective theory, in which the ALP couples to the Standard Model (SM) fermions through shift-invariant derivative interactions. In contrast to previous studies, where flavor violation arises solely from flavor-changing ALP couplings, we also include the contributions proportional to flavor-conserving ALP couplings, in which the flavor change is mediated by the weak interactions of the SM. Based on this analysis, we derive upper bounds on both flavor-changing and flavor-conserving ALP couplings at low energies. Then we consider the UV scenario of a "minimally flavor-violating ALP", which features flavor-universal ALP-fermion couplings at very high energies, and evaluate the resulting constraints on the UV couplings.

papers.title: The SymTFT and Quantum Phases of Matter
papers.abstract: The symmetry topological field theory (SymTFT) provides a unified framework for ordinary and generalized symmetries of quantum many-body systems. By encoding symmetry in a topological theory in one higher dimension, it separates symmetry data from the details of a specific quantum system. In this review, we give a pedagogical introduction to this framework and survey its applications to phases of quantum matter. For fusion category symmetries in ${(1+1)}$d, we explain how the SymTFT characterizes anomalies, classifies gapped phases, and organizes the symmetry structure of gapless phases. We also give a broad overview of further developments of this framework, including extensions to symmetries in higher dimensions, continuous symmetries, fermionic systems, mixed states, and spacetime symmetries.

papers.title: Plugging the Pion Chimney
papers.abstract: Heavy QCD axions and other gluon-coupled axion-like particles (ALPs) with masses from MeV to GeV are well motivated and have been searched for extensively. However, a window around the neutral pion mass, the so-called pion chimney, has escaped every search. There the ALP mixes strongly with the $π^0$ and therefore shares its experimental signatures. We show that the chimney can be closed with existing LHC data. The key point is that mixing changes the lifetimes of the two mass eigenstates but does not make them equal, and at LHC energies the states are boosted enough for the lifetime to decide whether they escape the detector or decay inside it. The ATLAS monojet search constrains the first case and the ATLAS inclusive photon measurement the second, and together they exclude the chimney up to the cutoff of the ALP effective theory. Above the cutoff, LHC searches for the colored states of the simplest ultraviolet completions exclude the rest. We also show that the bound from the $K^+$ width does not reach the chimney, because an ALP passes the same selection as a $π^0$, and we derive an independent, purely kinematic constraint from the measured $π^\pm$-$π^0$ mass splitting.

papers.title: Temporal polarization properties of accretion flows into supermassive black holes: INSANE as an alternative
papers.abstract: Temporal variability and polarization provide unique diagnostics of the magnetic field structure and plasma dynamics in accretion flows around supermassive black holes. We investigate the temporal polarization properties of horizon-scale emission using general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations coupled with polarized general relativistic radiative transfer (GRRT) for three accretion states: Standard and Normal Evolution (SANE), Magnetically Arrested Disk (MAD), and an intermediate regime (INSANE). Fourier polarization-mode decomposition, through the ratio $|β_m|/|β_2|$, shows that MAD produces the most rotationally symmetric EVPA patterns, SANE the most asymmetric, and INSANE lies in between. The multi-scale temporal behaviour of the intensity is investigated using the Continuous Wavelet Transform and Hilbert-Huang Transform. Both methods identify localized oscillatory features associated with magnetic-flux eruption events in the MAD simulations. In the shorter interval examined, INSANE distributes its variability more evenly among several time-scales, while the SANE behaviour depends more strongly on the electron-temperature prescription. To quantify the spectral distribution, we define a fast power fraction $F_{\mathrm{fast},I}$ for periods of 80-200 $M$ within a broad band of 80-1500 $M$. Both methods give the smallest fractions for MAD; the ordering of state medians, INSANE > SANE > MAD, persists when the upper fast-band boundary is varied from 200 to 500 $M$. Our analysis demonstrates that combining polarization morphology with multi-scale temporal analysis provides a useful means of distinguishing magnetization states, supporting INSANE as a distinct observational alternative to conventional MAD/SANE for interpreting horizon-scale observations of M87$^{*}$ and related systems.

papers.title: Velocity Reconstruction from kSZ with SPT-3G and DESI-LS
papers.abstract: We reconstruct the large-scale radial velocity field from the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect for the first time with the South Pole Telescope, and measure the galaxy-velocity correlation and the velocity power spectrum. We cross-correlate the SPT-3G D1 maps at 95, 150, and 220 GHz with luminous red galaxies from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys over the SPT-3G Main field. For the extended galaxy sample, we detect the galaxy-velocity correlation at signal-to-noise ratio $11.2$ and the velocity power spectrum at $8.1$, combining the three frequencies. We detect the reconstructed velocities for the first time at 220 GHz with signal-to-noise ratios of 4.2 and 3.1 from the galaxy-velocity correlation dipole and monopole, and at 3.8 from the velocity power spectrum. We model and estimate foreground contributions to the monopole, detecting both the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect and the cosmic infrared background contribution separately. On the around five percent of sky jointly covered by SPT-3G and DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys, reconstructed velocities give new constraints on local-type primordial non-Gaussianity at $f_{\rm NL}=-38^{+61}_{-61}$, and adding galaxy clustering gives $f_{\rm NL}=-20^{+40}_{-46}$. The galaxy-velocity correlation is consistent between the three frequencies.

papers.title: Depolarization of Synchrotron Polarization in Magnetized Interstellar Media
papers.abstract: We numerically study three key depolarization mechanisms of synchrotron polarization, including wavelength independent depolarization, differential Faraday rotation depolarization, and beam depolarization, across subAlfvénic and superAlfvénic turbulent regimes. Using 3D MHD simulations and synthetic observations, we analyze their effects on polarization degree and power spectra. We find that (1) SubAlfvénic turbulence shows high but strongly suppressed polarization under Faraday rotation, while superAlfvénic turbulence remains low and stable; (2) Differential Faraday depolarization dominates in ordered subAlfvénic media. For disordered superAlfvénic regimes, beam depolarization dominates at high frequencies, while at low frequencies it saturates and differential Faraday depolarization takes over as the dominant mechanism; and (3) Depolarization significantly distorts spectra in superAlfvénic turbulence but weakly affects subAlfvénic cases. Our results provide a quantitative basis for correcting depolarization biases in magnetic turbulence measurements with radio polarization data.

papers.abstract: We propose using hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession experiments, traditionally employed in precision frequency measurements and searches for the electron electric dipole moment, as complementary probes of light scalar-mediated, spin-dependent fifth forces. We investigate their sensitivity to Lorentz-violating interactions mediated by scalars with masses ranging from $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4}~μ\mathrm{eV})$ to $\mathcal{O}(10~\mathrm{keV})$. While hydrogen maser spectroscopy and molecular spin-precession measurements probe different combinations of Lorentz-violating couplings, we find that the strongest projected sensitivities can be achieved using spin-precession of ultracold molecules, benefiting from their extended coherence times. These experimental approaches provide access to previously unexplored regions of parameter space, probing interaction ranges extending from centimeter to sub-angstrom scales. Our proposals highlight the potential of precision atomic and molecular experiments to search for new spin-dependent scalar-mediated interactions and violations of fundamental spacetime symmetries.

papers.title: Solar atmospheric gravity wave phase differences: insights from MANCHA simulations and observations
papers.abstract: Phase-difference and coherence diagnostics are widely used to identify gravity waves in the solar atmosphere, but their sensitivity to opacity and radiative-transfer effects remains poorly understood. We investigate the robustness of gravity-wave signatures in velocity and temperature diagnostics and their appearance in spectroscopic observables. We perform k-/omega phase-difference and coherence analyses using three-dimensional radiative hydrodynamic simulations with the MANCHA code. Diagnostics are evaluated at constant geometrical heights and optical depths. Synthetic Fe I 6173 Å profiles provide bisector velocities, continuum intensities, and line-core intensities. We also analyse high-resolution quiet-Sun observations from the 1-m Swedish Solar Telescope (SST). Velocity diagnostics show similar phase differences and coherence at both sampling levels, including those derived from synthetic and observed bisector velocities, indicating their relative insensitivity to the sampling method. In contrast, temperature diagnostics show stronger and more extended gravity-wave signatures at fixed geometrical height. Synthetic continuum and line-core intensities retain these signatures but exhibit phase differences more closely resembling temperature diagnostics at constant optical depth. SST observations show similar qualitative behaviour, despite quantitative differences. Our results demonstrate that Doppler velocity provides a relatively robust diagnostic of gravity-wave phase propagation, whereas temperature and intensity diagnostics are more sensitive to opacity and radiative-transfer effects. Consequently, the latter may introduce biases in estimates of wave propagation speeds and energy fluxes.

papers.title: Efficient and Optimal Analysis of Galaxy Surveys on Large Scales
papers.abstract: On sufficiently large scales the galaxy overdensity field is approximately Gaussian, so its information can be losslessly compressed into the power spectrum. Standard power spectrum estimators are nevertheless suboptimal on the largest scales, where the survey window induces significant coupling between different modes. Optimal power spectrum analysis typically requires an inverse of the covariance matrix, which can be overly expensive. Here we develop an alternative field level approach, which is significantly faster. We assess its impact on constraining primordial non-Gaussianity of the local type, which is particularly sensitive to these largest scales. Relative to the standard power spectrum analysis, our field level likelihood forecasts a $14\%$ improvement in constraining power. For the DESI DR2 LRG and QSO samples, our approach forecasts $σ(f_{\rm NL})=4.1$, compared to $σ(f_{\rm NL})=4.8$ from the power spectrum based analysis. The field level approach also enables efficient implementations of additional non-cosmological contributions to the signal. As an example, we present a novel non-parametric method to mitigate angular systematics, enabling efficient deprojection of contaminated modes.

papers.title: Flavor-dependent quark-mass scaling and the fate of the strange-matter window in self-bound quark stars
papers.abstract: In the flavor-dependent QMDD model, self-bound $ud$ quark matter can be the ground state at vanishing pressure and convert into $uds$ matter through a first-order transition. So far the mass functional has used parameters $(a,C)$ common to all flavors; here we let the strange sector have its own coupling, $C_s=α\,C_{u,d}$, and map the response of the zero-pressure parameter space. The $e^0_{ud}=930\,$MeV boundary is independent of $α$ by construction, whereas increasing $α$ enlarges the self-bound $ud$ domain and pushes the $e^0_{ud}=e^0_{uds}$ line towards larger $a$. The causality boundary $c^0_s=c$ is almost frozen near $a\simeq5.5$. The competition closes the strange-matter window at \RA{$α_{\rm crit}\simeq1.136$}: above it every causal self-bound parametrization is $ud$ at zero pressure, so a first-order $ud\!\to\!uds$ transition must occur at higher pressure, though not necessarily inside a star, since the maximum mass may be reached below the transition density. The transition pressure and the energy-density jump grow monotonically with $α$, both scale \RB{approximately} with the available-volume fraction $q=1-κ$, and the Seidov onset-instability diagnostic stays below unity.

papers.title: Complexity and symmetry: The asymmetry factor approach
papers.abstract: We study the influence of the instantaneous appearance of a time-like Killing vector (TKV) in self-gravitating fluid spheres during their evolution. For doing so we resort to the concept of asymmetry factor which allows the existence of any specific type of symmetry (e.g. a TKV), exclusively, for a given value of the time-like coordinate. We consider adiabatic and dissipative fluids. The analysis of different relevant physical variables in this process shows the imprints of the emergence of TKV at some point of the evolution. Particular attention is paid to the relationship appearing between the TKV, and the complexity factor describing the degree of complexity of the fluid, bringing out for the first time a link between complexity and symmetry.

papers.title: Cataclysmic Variables from XMM-Newton and eROSITA
papers.abstract: Cataclysmic variables (CVs) are interacting binaries where a white dwarf accretes material from a late-type donor. The most evolved systems, referred to as period-bouncers, host degenerate donors. We present XMM-Newton and eROSITA, which provide complementary views of the CV population. We summarize the capabilities of XMM-Newton for timing and spectroscopic studies, and its ability to characterize accretion geometries, magnetic field strengths, and short-term variability across magnetic/non-magnetic CVs. These data allow studies of individual systems, including magnetic period-bouncers with soft X-ray spectra and faint luminosities that offer insights into the late stages of CV evolution. We then present an overview of eROSITA as the first X-ray all-sky survey in the soft band since ROSAT, and its impact on population studies. The eRASS:4 catalog expands the known X-ray sky and will enable volume-limited samples of CVs, complete up to 500pc for standard CVs and up to 250 pc for period-bouncers. Cross-matching eROSITA detections with optical catalogs produced the largest sample of X-ray-selected CV candidates to date, that will refine X-ray diagnostic diagrams, reassess the demographics of magnetic/non-magnetic systems, and identify new highly evolved CVs. Finally, we describe ongoing searches for unknown systems, including CVs selected through probabilistic cross-matching with Gaia, and period-bouncers identified through a multi-wavelength scorecard. These efforts led to the discovery of new period-bouncers and a promising detached period-bouncer candidate, that could validate alternative models for the evolution of CVs. Together, XMM-Newton and eROSITA provide an unprecedented view into the structure, evolution, and demographics of CVs, with eROSITA laying the groundwork for future studies of compact binary evolution, the Galactic Ridge X-ray emission, and related phenomena.

papers.title: A Predictive Nuclear Effective Field Theory from Wilsonian Renormalization Group Principles I: Medium-mass nuclei and nuclear matter
papers.abstract: The predictive power of nuclear effective field theory (EFT) from few- to many-body systems is substantially restricted by regulator dependence. Wilsonian momentum-shell renormalization group (RG) offers a natural framework for cutoff-independent predictions, but its many-body implementation requires regulating single-particle momentum modes, which breaks Galilean invariance. RG scaling analysis shows that this symmetry breaking is encoded in irrelevant operators whose effects can be included explicitly or absorbed into higher-body interactions. Guided by Wilsonian RG, we construct a regularization scheme for chiral EFT contact interactions and predict binding energies of nuclei up to $^{40}$Ca using interactions calibrated only to $A\leq3$ systems. The predicted energies vary at the percent level and agree with experiment for $300\leqΛ\leq450$~MeV. The same scheme reduces the overbinding of symmetric nuclear matter obtained with conventional relative-momentum regulators. Our results suggest that some model dependence observed in nonrelativistic many-body calculations originates from treating EFT vertices as static, Galilean-invariant potentials rather than as field operators regulated consistently across particle-number sectors.

papers.title: ASAS-SN Rates V: Tidal Disruption Event Volumetric Rates and Luminosity Functions by Optical Spectroscopic Type, X-ray Luminosity, and Host-Galaxy Properties
papers.abstract: We present volumetric rates and luminosity functions (LFs) of tidal disruption events (TDEs) based on 21 TDEs from the All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae (ASAS-SN) between 2014 and 2024. We calculate completeness corrections from injection-recovery simulations of the ASAS-SN light curves using individual TDE templates. We find a total volumetric rate of $\log_{10}(R_{\rm tot}[{\rm yr}^{-1}{\rm Gpc}^{-3}h_{70}^3]) = 2.32^{+0.15}_{-0.23}$ for $z \leq 0.12$. We also measure the rates of two growing TDE subpopulations. The one off-nuclear TDE in our standard sample implies $\log_{10}(R_{\rm off\text{-}nuclear}) = 0.39^{+0.52}_{-0.76}$ ($1.2^{+3.4}_{-1.0}$% of the total rate). We measure the rate of recurrent TDEs (rTDEs) to be $\log_{10}(R_{\rm recurrent}) = 1.26^{+0.23}_{-0.62}$ ($9^{+8}_{-6}$% of the total rate) from the four rTDEs in our standard sample, increasing to $1.45^{+0.20}_{-0.35}$ ($13^{+10}_{-7}$%) when the well-studied ASASSN-14ko is included. Galaxies with substantial (>0.1%) burst-mass fractions and steeply falling star-formation histories host the majority of TDEs. We recover the known overrepresentation of TDEs in post-starburst galaxies, by a factor of $15^{+16}_{-11}$ relative to matched control galaxies, and a weaker enhancement of $5^{+5}_{-4}$ in quiescent Balmer-strong galaxies. TDE-H+He events dominate the volumetric TDE rate, with TDE-H, TDE-He, and TDE-Featureless events comprising <15% of nearby TDEs. The $g$-band LFs are statistically indistinguishable when split at the median X-ray to UV/optical blackbody luminosity ratio of $\sim$1%, corroborating unification models where the observed multi-wavelength emission is set primarily by viewing angle effects. Extrapolating the measured TDE LFs to higher luminosities and more massive black holes supports a TDE origin for luminous ambiguous nuclear transients and extreme nuclear transients.

papers.title: Convergence of the quasinormal-mode expansion of the Kerr Green function
papers.abstract: Black-hole ringdown is usually modeled as a linear superposition of quasinormal modes, and fits to gravitational-wave observations increasingly include high overtones. However, the overtone sum does not necessarily converge: overtones are more strongly damped and thus decay faster in time, but their amplitudes in the Green function (the signal at an observer produced by an impulse at a source point) grow, so the mode description may break down before a finite time. We show that for a rotating (Kerr) black hole this time has a clear geometric meaning. For highly damped modes, the amplitudes grow exponentially with the optical distance from the source and the observer to a characteristic "bounce" radius close to the black hole, defined as the location where the mode amplitude is smallest. For one family of modes, the amplitudes are also suppressed the farther the source and observer sit from the equatorial plane. Rotation therefore makes the onset of convergence depend on direction as well as distance, extending the geometric picture from bounce radii to bounce surfaces. Combining these effects gives a sufficient condition for absolute convergence. For spin $a/M = 0.7$, we map how this time varies with source and observer position, and amplitudes computed numerically reproduce the predicted spatial dependence to better than one percent. These results set geometric limits on when the quasinormal-mode sums converge.

papers.title: oMEGACat-JWST I.: Project description and photometric data release
papers.abstract: Omega Centauri (NGC 5139, $ω$ Cen) is the most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way and the likely stripped nucleus of an accreted dwarf galaxy. Extensive HST observations have uncovered many of its peculiar features, including complex subpopulations and kinematic evidence for an intermediate-mass black hole via central fast-moving stars. High-precision astrometric follow-up is essential to constrain the orbits of these stars. We present oMEGACat-JWST, a deep photometric and astrometric catalog of $ω$ Cen's core and surroundings that extends our previous oMEGACat efforts to near-infrared wavelengths. The superior sensitivity and angular resolution of the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provide significant astrometric and photometric improvements, particularly for faint stars. Our catalog is based on a custom reduction of NIRCam and NIRISS imaging across three JWST programs extending out to two half-light radii (10'). In total, our catalog contains approximately 677 000 sources. In the region overlapping with oMEGACat, we achieve high relative completeness (> 90% of HST sources recovered) while detecting over 86 000 new sources below HST's detection limit. Astrometric tests demonstrate a single-image precision as good as 0.5% of a NIRCam pixel (0.15 mas) at mF115W=18; at mF115W=23 the precision is still 1 mas. Color-magnitude diagrams based on our data show the well-known split between the primordial Helium and the Helium enriched populations and are particularly sensitive to light-element (CNO) variations of faint stars. oMEGACat-JWST provides the most complete photometric catalog of $ω$ Cen's core to date. Combined with HST data, it enables multi-wavelength subpopulation analyses. Together with future monitoring observations, its high astrometric precision will improve our understanding of the kinematics of the central fast-moving stars in $ω$ Cen.

papers.title: Low-state X-ray spectra of magnetized neutron stars: Probing accretion regimes in SFXTs
papers.abstract: Supergiant fast X-ray transients (SFXTs) are a subclass of high-mass X-ray binaries characterized by prolonged quiescent states, making them ideal sources for studying accretion onto highly magnetized neutron stars (NSs) at low rates. In this work, we present a broadband spectral analysis of three SFXTs: IGR J16418$-$4532, IGR J17544$-$2619, and IGR J11215$-$5952, using archival $XMM-Newton$, NICER, and $ NuSTAR$ observations. Joint spectral fitting of the NICER and $NuSTAR$ data for IGR J16418$-$4532 confirms the presence of a cyclotron resonant scattering feature (CRSF) at $\sim 50$ keV, implying a NS magnetic field strength of $\sim 6\times10^{12}$ G. We detect a cyclotron line at $\sim27$ keV in IGR J17544$-$2619, significantly higher than the previously reported energy of $\sim17$ keV, a difference that may reflect luminosity-dependent changes in the accretion flow. Using a double-Comptonization model, we identify the characteristic two-hump spectral shape in IGR J16418$-$4532 and IGR J17544$-$2619 at luminosities $\lesssim10^{35}$ $\rm erg\,s^{-1}$, indicating that this spectral transition is a universal feature of accreting magnetized NSs independent of the source type. Furthermore, the ratio between the cyclotron line energy and the intersection energy of the two humps in both sources is consistent with the empirical relation established in Be/X-ray binaries, suggesting that the overheated polar cap atmosphere model used to explain X-ray pulsars in low-luminosity states is also applicable to SFXTs. In contrast, IGR J11215$-$5952 shows a smooth single-component spectrum at all flux levels, which indicates a relatively weak magnetic field of the NS.

papers.title: Search for the low-mass isotropic signature of QCD instantons in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV using the ATLAS detector
papers.abstract: This Letter presents the first search for QCD instanton-induced events at the LHC. Instantons are semi-classical solutions of the Yang-Mills equations of QCD and correspond to non-perturbative tunneling between topologically distinct vacuum sectors. The search is performed in 1.6 $\text{nb}^{-1}$ of very low instantaneous luminosity proton-proton collision data collected by the ATLAS detector at 13 TeV. Angular variables based on reconstructed charged-particle tracks are used to discriminate the expected rest-frame isotropy of low-mass instanton events from the minimum-bias background. The minimum-bias event background is predicted using a data-driven technique and reweighted Monte Carlo models. A profile-likelihood fit is performed in a two-dimensional classifier variable to extract a possible signal contribution, yielding an excess of low-mass isotropic events with an observed significance of $3.5σ$.

papers.title: A refined upper bound on the critical temperature for dilute Bose gases
papers.abstract: We establish an upper bound on the critical temperature shift of three-dimensional Bose gases with general nonnegative finite-range interactions. In the dilute regime $aρ^{1/3}\to0$, we prove $T_c(ρ)/T_c^{(0)}(ρ) \le 1 + (C_{\rm H}+o(1))\sqrt{aρ^{1/3}}$, where \[ C_{\rm H}=\frac{2^{7/2}\sqrtπ}{3ζ(3/2)^{2/3}} =3.523992\ldots \] is the coefficient predicted by Huang in 1999. This improves the earlier rigorous upper bound of Seiringer and Ueltschi in 2009. More precisely, we prove the exponential decay of the correlations above the stated temperature through the Feynman--Kac representation, for both integrable and hard-core interactions.

papers.title: New Historical Guest-Star Candidates from Reassessed Chinese Records: Lunar Occultation of Planets
papers.abstract: Ancient Chinese records of lunar occultations of planets have been used to test planetary theories and investigate long-term changes in Earth's rotation. However, certain records contain identification errors whose origins remain poorly understood; we propose that some of these errors may arise from misidentifying guest stars, such as novae or supernovae, as planets. We analyzed 67 errata on lunar occultations of planets from Liu Ci-Yuan's (2015) monograph using modern ephemerides and the open-source Python package \texttt{occultsky}, publicly available on GitHub. Using recorded dates and dynastic capital coordinates, we constructed observing windows anchored at solar noon and extending by $\pm 1$ day. Each window covered the preceding and recorded nights because the date may be off by one day. For each of the 67 records, we cataloged the apparent right ascension and declination $(α, δ)$ at the midpoint of the Moon's visibility window on each candidate night. The band swept by the lunar disk confines a possible transient to a narrow region a few degrees across; these midpoint coordinates serve as proxies for the implied guest-star positions. The catalog supplies candidate positions rather than identifications, enabling remnant and compact-object searches to test the guest-star hypothesis directly. If associations are established, these records could become dated guest-star candidates, and their dates could anchor remnant ages.

papers.title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at multi-TeV muon colliders
papers.abstract: We investigate the sensitivity of future multi-TeV muon colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton within the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We consider $τ^+τ^-$ production through $μ^+μ^-$ annihilation and vector-boson scattering, electroweak-boson-associated $τ$ production, and the radiative Higgs decay $H\toτ^+τ^-γ$. At high energies, the dipole-induced contributions quadratic in the Wilson coefficients become particularly important, with associated Higgs production, $μ^+μ^-\toτ^+τ^-H$, providing the strongest sensitivity through energy-enhanced contact interactions. The remaining channels offer complementary probes of the underlying dipole operators. For a $10$~TeV muon collider with an integrated luminosity of $10\,\mathrm{ab}^{-1}$, we obtain combined sensitivities at the nominal $95\%$ confidence level of $|Δa_τ|<1.2\times10^{-5}$, $|d_τ|<6.6\times10^{-20}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$, $|Δa_τ^Z|<1.8\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_τ^Z|<1.0\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$. Compared with FCC-ee projections, the muon collider offers substantially stronger sensitivity to the electric dipole moments, while both facilities offer complementary probes of magnetic dipole moments. These results motivate further studies incorporating realistic detector effects and systematic uncertainties.

papers.title: Loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ at NLO+PS for LHC simulations: exact, fast scale and PDF event weights, theory uncertainties, and the limits of rescaled LO+PS
papers.abstract: We study loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ production with charged-lepton and neutrino $Z$ decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD matched to parton showers, using public software at $\sqrt{s}=13$ and 13.6 TeV. An exact loop-amplitude cache reduces event-generation time by a factor of 26 with 450 scale and PDF weights, while Born suppression improves boosted-event statistics without changing the weighted prediction. We present inclusive results for both channels and charged-lepton differential and STXS Stage 1.3 predictions with theory uncertainties. At 13.6 TeV, fixed-order top-quark mass-scheme variations transferred to NLO+PS dominate the statistically precise central-Higgs STXS bins for $p_\mathrm{T}^V\ge150$ GeV, reaching 32-50%. An inclusive $K$ factor does not reproduce the boosted and jet-dependent NLO+PS spectra of the tested LO+PS samples, and the differences depend strongly on the shower prescription. For specified CMS- and ATLAS-style vetoed sources at 13.6 TeV, we construct separate charged-lepton and neutrino corrections using ensembles of gradient-boosted classifiers, with calibration, target-theory variations and transfer uncertainties. Independent tests show substantial improvement over inclusive rescaling in most tested distributions, but not uniform closure. In charged-lepton calibration comparisons, the median STXS uncertainty from transported NLO scales and transfer terms is 17% for both the CMS- and ATLAS-style corrections, compared with LO scale uncertainties of 28% and 26% at fixed $K$. These comparisons do not include the complete target-theory budget. The corrections do not restore the depleted hard-recoil population; the highest ATLAS-style $p_\mathrm{T}^H$ bin stays below NLO+PS even at the upper edge of its band. The setup, reference results, and source- and channel-specific models support new NLO+PS generation and reuse of existing samples within stated limits.

papers.title: Gravity/Thermodynamics Correspondence for Generic Dynamical Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Working within covariant phase space formalism, we establish \textit{gravity-thermodynamics correspondence} for generic dynamical spacetimes. We derive local first and second laws of thermodynamics on general null boundaries, for generic non-stationary solutions to Einstein gravity {with minimally coupled matter} for physical observers that we carefully specify. Entropy variation, which receives contribution only from the gravitational sector, is the surface charge variation associated with a vector field generating the null boundary, and temperature is its non-affinity parameter (divided by $2π$). The statement of the second law in our setting is that the entropy variation evaluated along the null vector field is strictly non-negative for the admissible positive-non-affinity clock and matter satisfying the null energy condition. Our dynamical entropy variation, which is non-integrable for generic non-stationary solutions, becomes integrable in near-stationary configurations, reproducing the Hollands--Wald--Zhang dynamical entropy formula. Strikingly, this local second law holds even when the boundary area is decreasing, disentangling thermodynamic irreversibility and the second law from standard area theorems. Our first-principles construction demonstrates that gravitational thermodynamics requires neither a stationary background, teleological event horizons, nor an exact entropy state function on individual codimension-1 spacelike slices of the null boundary (codimension two in spacetime).

papers.title: Resolving Individual Massive Stars in an M31 Star Cluster Exhibiting Wolf-Rayet Features
papers.abstract: The observed ratio of Wolf-Rayet (WR) star subtypes (e.g., WC/WN) in M31 is significantly higher than the predictions of standard stellar evolution models, yet this key diagnostic discrepancy remains unresolved. This is partly due to incomplete census and the challenge of resolving individual stars in compact clusters with ground-based telescopes. In this work, we report a young cluster with WR features with the (R.A., Dec) = (00:43:39.36, +41:10:08.7), discovered with LAMOST spectra. We use the high spatial resolution of the HST imaging data to resolve the cluster members, leading to the identification of four WR star candidates, four OB stars, and one yellow supergiant. Based on the current known WR sample in M31 observed in the HST F275W filter, about one-third of WRs are contaminated by other sources within a 1. "1 $\times$ 1. "1 aperture, while this fraction can reach up to two-thirds for the LAMOST fiber size of 3. "3. Applying the approach demonstrated in this work to a larger sample of crowded regions in M31 will yield a more complete census and allow for the measurement of a definitive WC/WN ratio, corrected for contamination. Whether this refined ratio increases or decreases the current tension with models remains to be seen, but it will provide the essential observational constraint needed to advance our understanding.

papers.title: A Catalog of Young Stellar Objects in the Lagoon Nebula
papers.abstract: M8, the Lagoon Nebula, has been known for more than 100 years as a region forming stars. It is (in projection) very close to if not in the Galactic Bulge. As a result, the source surface density is very high and source confusion is a substantial challenge. Because of the location, there have been many surveys that serendipitously observed M8, in addition to studies specifically targeting it. But to this point, there has been no effort to resolve source confusion across all the existing catalogs, spanning many different wavelengths, sensitivities, and spatial resolutions. We have done all of this source reconciliation, and present the merged catalog here. The net result is 3019 YSOs with largely photometric data and/or YSO selection from ~50 different origins, primarily ranging from $g$-band through 25 um, but with a significant number of X-ray sources, and some data of limited sensitivity out through 70-450 um. The catalog includes several flags that enable users to select, e.g., the YSOs that have been identified as young by the most studies, or the YSOs with the most multi-wavelength counterparts, or the ones with the clearest IR excesses. We use this catalog in a companion paper; it will also be of use in, e.g., future SPHEREx and Roman work.

papers.title: Giant gravitons without giant gravitons
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that the partition function of a free bosonic $U(N)$ multi-matrix model admits a giant graviton expansion. For $d$ matrices, there are $d$ distinct giant gravitons, and the expansion can be characterized by a $d$-node quiver with bifundamentals connecting the nodes. This suggests the intriguing possibility of a more generalized holography where models without any obvious gravitational dual can nevertheless be given a dual brane interpretation. The giant graviton expansion of this multi-matrix model is somewhat unconventional though, as the giant graviton partition functions will necessarily have intrinsic $N$-dependence.

papers.title: Brown dwarfs and stars are dynamically indistinguishable as companions in AU-separation binaries
papers.abstract: Brown dwarfs occupy the mass range between stars and planets, populations whose dominant formation channels differ, which leave measurable differences in the orbital eccentricity and host-star metallicity distributions. We assemble a sample of astrometric binaries with main sequence primaries and brown dwarf companions at $\mathcal{O}$(AU) separations from $\textit{Gaia}$ DR3. The observable photocenter motions for such binaries are degenerate between a genuinely low-mass companion and a near-equal-mass binary. We break this degeneracy using $\textit{Gaia}$ XP spectrophotometry and follow-up FEROS spectroscopy, which removes removes ${\sim}70\%$ of initial low-mass-function candidates as likely near-twin binaries and leaves residual contamination of only a few percent. The resulting 368 systems, with masses and metallicities determined from the XP spectra and a selection function forward-modelled with $\texttt{Gaiamock}$, form the largest homogeneous sample of brown dwarf companions with astrometric orbits. We find the eccentricity distribution to be well described by a normal distribution. This is comparable to eccentricities of stellar companions at the same periods and higher than those of giant planets, with no significant dependence on companion mass ($α=-0.13\pm0.09$) or period ($β=0.10\pm0.05$). The host-star metallicity distribution is likewise stellar-like, extending to [M/H]$=-0.5$, in contrast to the predominantly super-solar metallicity hosts of giant planets. After accounting for selection, the companion-mass distribution over all brown dwarf masses is consistent with an extension of stellar-binary demographics. Brown dwarf companions at AU separations down to at least $20\,M_J$ therefore appear to form predominantly through a binary-star-like channel. A possible transition to planet-like formation at lower masses cannot be located with the present sample.

papers.title: Search for UHE photon sources using direction-time clustering algorithms with a BDT particle discriminant
papers.abstract: Direction-time clustering methods for neutral particle searches are motivated by the possibility that ultra-high-energy (UHE) neutral particles are produced during flaring periods of various astrophysical sources. In this scenario, clusters of events correlated in both arrival direction and time would be generated, which, when observed, would indicate a neutral-particle flare, and a non-observation would provide upper limits on fluxes for point-like sources. Focusing on UHE photon searches, an improvement of the sensitivity of direction-time clustering methods by the application of different photon tags, such as the depth of the extensive air shower maximum (X_max), the lateral distribution of the total signal across an array of detectors (S_b), or a cumulative signal trace-based discriminant variable (C_t), is investigated. A Boosted Decision Tree (BDT) is used to combine multiple observables, by which photon tagging is optimized and photon/hadron separation is improved. The number of events required to identify a photon flare is thereby further reduced compared to using individual photon tags, across a range of flare durations. The possibility of extending the known and assumed PeVatron photon sources into the UHE regime by applying these clustering methods to existing and future observatory data is also discussed. The discovery of UHE neutral particles would mark the next milestone in multimessenger astrophysics, by which a new window onto the non-thermal universe would be opened.

papers.title: An exact separability criterion for the $J/ψΛ$ spin state in $Λ_b^0\to J/ψ\,Λ$ decays at the LHC

Within the four-amplitude family $\{a_\pm,b_\pm\}$, the system is separable if and only if $(1+P_b\cosθ)a_+b_+=(1-P_b\cosθ)a_-b_-=P_b\sinθb_+b_-=0$, where $θ$ is the $Λ$ production angle defined in the LHC environment. We propose a profiled likelihood ratio test to probe entanglement in the full five-dimensional angular analysis. Idealized pseudoexperiments compare this test with a negativity test and a test based on the angular moments $M_7$ and $M_9$ for rejecting the $a_+=b_-=0$ hypothesis. At both $3σ$ and $5σ$ significance, the proposed test achieves a $90\%$ rejection power with about half as many signal events as the other two methods. These results support the prospects for entanglement evidence with samples on the existing scale and for observation with larger samples.

papers.title: On the Structure of the Nuclear-Clock Isotope $^{229}$Th Beyond Quadratic Order
papers.abstract: Precision measurements of the exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition of $^{229}$Th, offer an extraordinary sensitivity to a variety of new light fields. However, interpreting such measurements requires nuclear-structure information beyond what is currently constrained by spectroscopy. We develop a systematic description of the electric multipole interactions governing the hyperfine structure of ${}^{229}$Th, including the hexadecapole contribution, and perform a symmetry-based analysis of the resulting hyperfine splittings in crystalline environments. Hyperfine spectroscopy generally constrains combinations of nuclear moments and crystal-field gradients, leading to degeneracies when higher multipole interactions are allowed. We then combine experimental nuclear observables, particle-rotor relations, and a deformed-Fermi charge-density model to investigate the electromagnetic contribution to the nuclear clock's sensitivity to variations in the fine-structure constant. We find that higher-order nuclear deformation and state-dependent differences in the radial charge distribution of the clock states can substantially alter the predicted sensitivity, introducing large uncertainties that are not constrained by existing measurements. Our results highlight the importance of combining nuclear and solid-state theory with complementary measurements, including spectroscopy of higher-spin states, to constrain the nuclear structure and improve predictions of the clock's sensitivity to new physics. Our symmetry-based analysis also provides a framework for using hyperfine spectroscopy to investigate local defect symmetries in crystalline hosts.

papers.title: Perturbative QCD Analysis for the Electric Dipole Moment of $Ξ$ and $Σ$ Hyperons from CP-Violating Dipole Interactions
papers.abstract: Hyperon electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe CP-violating interactions beyond the Standard Model. Motivated by the recent BESIII measurement [Ablikim et al., Science 393, 1027] and the perturbative QCD analysis of the $Λ$ EDM form factor $d_Λ$ [Chen et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 051902], we extend the perturbative QCD calculation of the EDM form factor to the $Ξ$ and $Σ$ hyperons. We derive factorization formulas from quark EDM and chromoelectric dipole moment contributions in terms of leading-twist light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs). Using lattice-QCD results for the LCDAs and the strange-quark dipole moment ranges inferred from the BESIII $d_Λ$ bound and neutron EDM constraints, we obtain the conditional estimates $-4.8 \times 10^{-18} < d_{Ξ^-} < 1.8\times10^{-18}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $-6.1\times10^{-19} < d_{Σ^+} < 2.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,\mathrm{cm}$ at the scale of ${J/ψ}$ mass. Dedicated searches at BESIII and the future Super Tau-Charm Factory could further constrain these quark-level sources of CP violation.

papers.title: Flash UV Spectroscopy: Decoding the Ultraviolet Diversity of Young Core-Collapse Supernovae with the Hubble Space Telescope
papers.abstract: We present multi-wavelength observations and modeling of the largest sample to date of core-collapse supernovae (SNe) with Hubble Space Telescope (HST) ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy within < 2 weeks of first light. Our total sample contains early-time UV spectroscopy from 12 Type II SNe (SNe II), 3 Type IIb SNe (SNe IIb), 3 Type IIn SNe (SNe IIn) and 1 Type I super-luminous SN (SLSN-I). This sample includes 11 objects with unpublished UV spectroscopy from HST Cycles 31 and 32 "Flexible Thursdays" target of opportunity programs, increasing the number of core-collapse SNe with early-time HST UV spectra by a factor of 2.4. The early-time near-UV spectra of most sample SNe II show similar Doppler-broadened P-Cygni profiles of metals (Mg, Fe, Ti, Cr), though with notable diversity in line velocities and absorption strengths. Comparison to non-Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (nLTE) radiative transfer model grids at similar phases indicates that most sample SNe II are consistent with low circumstellar material (CSM) densities at the time of UV observations (e.g., $\dot M = 10^{-6}$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$, $v_w = 50$ km/s) and standard kinetic energies (e.g., $E_k = 0.6-1.2$ B), while two objects, SNe 2024faq and 2023ixf, show UV/optical evidence for interaction with more confined, higher-density CSM. SN 2023ixf and sample SNe IIn exhibit relatively featureless early-time UV spectra despite displaying prominent optical Lorentzian emission lines from electron scattering in optically thick CSM -- this being attributed to differing properties of UV resonance versus optical recombination transitions as well as intrinsic CSM asymmetries. These results demonstrate the potential of early-time UV spectroscopy to constrain the outermost SN ejecta structure, explosion energetics/composition, and progenitor mass-loss histories of core-collapse SNe.

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.abstract: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.

papers.title: A comprehensive Sun-as-a-star catalog of interplanetary type-III bursts: Statistics and a framework for stellar exospace weather applications
papers.abstract: Decameter-hectometric (DH) type-III bursts, produced by energetic electron beams escaping into interplanetary (IP) space, are often associated with strong soft X-ray (SXR) flares, coronal mass ejections (CMEs), and solar energetic particle events (SEPEs). With future DH missions being planned, these intense bursts could provide reliable exospace weather event diagnostics, given the lack of direct stellar IP particle and CME probes. We present a catalog of DH type-III bursts associated with 538 out of 734 $\geq$C5-class flares observed by Wind and STEREO spacecraft during 2006-2025. Independent of the SXR flare strength, the occurrence and Sun-as-a-star emission properties of DH type-III bursts distinguish confined flares, CMEs with and without strong IP shocks, and SEPEs. We find that logistic-regression models combining SXR and type-III properties provide more accurate and well-calibrated CME/SEPE occurrence probabilities than a model based only on SXR parameters. Further, a space weather event probability-estimation model based on physically meaningful, scale-free parameters derived from SXR and type-III properties outperforms an SXR parameter-only model. This result presents a way to define solar-calibrated exospace weather prediction models extendable to stellar flares with a range of energy scales but similar underlying physics. We also present a catalog of 26 shock-associated type-III (S-type-III) bursts that appear to start from cotemporal DH type-II bursts and are generally associated with fast halo CMEs and major SEPEs. Our catalogs and the scale-free model form a benchmark for exospace weather studies.

papers.title: Long-Term Spectral and Timing Variability of PKS 2155$-$304 from {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} Observations
papers.abstract: Blazars exhibit strong variability across the electromagnetic spectrum, on timescales from minutes to decades. We present a study of the spectral and timing variability of the TeV blazar PKS~2155$-$304 using {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} observations spanning 25 years (1999$-$2024). Timing analysis reveals fractional variability amplitudes of up to $F_{\rm var}\approx 24\%$ in the hard X-ray band and $F_{\rm var}\lesssim 7.5\%$ in the soft X-ray band, along with variable power-spectral indices across observations. The minimum variability timescale, $τ_{\rm var} = 1.15\pm0.26$~ks, limits the size of the X-ray emitting region to $R \lesssim 7.7 \times 10^{14}$~cm, consistent with synchrotron emission from a compact region in the jet. We fitted the spectra using power-law (PL), broken power-law (BPL), log-parabola (LP), and bremsstrahlung plus power-law (BR+PL) models, the latter used only as a phenomenological description of the spectral curvature. The BPL model provides the best statistical description for most {\it Chandra} spectra. An F-test confirms a curved model over PL for all {\it Chandra} spectra, whereas most {\it NuSTAR} spectra are consistent with a single PL. Hardness ratio analysis shows a harder-when-brighter trend in the {\it Chandra} band. Joint fitting of the simultaneous 2013 {\it Chandra} and {\it NuSTAR} observations shows that the broadband 0.4$-$79~keV curvature is confined to the soft X-ray band, with the spectrum steepening above $\sim$2~keV and a steep hard X-ray power law ($Γ\simeq 2.7$). Our results reveal energy-dependent X-ray variability over more than two decades, and show that broadband X-ray coverage is needed to locate the curvature of the synchrotron tail in high-synchrotron-peaked blazars.

papers.title: Euclid DR1 Legacy Science on Ultracool Dwarfs: Halpha activity, kinematic age and rotation of M7--L1 dwarfs from DESI DR1, SPHEREx and Euclid
papers.abstract: The fraction of late-M dwarfs with detectable Halpha rises toward the stellar-substellar boundary while their emission weakens relative to the bolometric luminosity, a contrast attributed to the fading continuum. We measure how much of this rise the continuum explains and whether younger populations or longer activity lifetimes contribute. We select 8939 dwarfs of type M7 or later, all but 22 of them M7-L1, from DESI DR1. We compare active fractions at common thresholds in equivalent width and in log(L_Ha/L_bol), the Halpha-to-bolometric luminosity ratio, in spectra sensitive to each threshold. We jointly model continuum fading, emission weakening and an extra active component. Kinematics use Gaia astrometry and DESI radial velocities for dwarfs with G < 19, free of proper-motion selection. From M7 to M9 the active fraction rises by 28 points at 5 Angstrom equivalent width. At log(L_Ha/L_bol) = -4.5 it falls by 23.5 points. SPHEREx and photometric bolometric fluxes agree within 0.03 dex. Joint fits require M8 emission to be 0.12-0.15 dex weaker than at M7. The brighter M8 dwarfs require an extra active component; the larger sample at most marginally. At log(L_Ha/L_bol) = -4.7, inactive M7 and M8 dwarfs have larger velocity dispersions than active ones. The measured rotators, mostly M6-M7 dwarfs, have saturated Halpha. Euclid DR1 NISP spectra of 152 M7-L1 dwarfs (144 at S/N >= 5) test the optical type scale, and VIS images resolve three close binaries (0.22-0.53 arcsec) with common proper motion. We confirm that the rise in equivalent-width incidence comes mostly from the fading continuum acting on weakening emission. Conditional on an age-velocity relation and uniform ages, a step model gives thin-disk activity lifetimes at log(L_Ha/L_bol) = -4.7 of 5.9 (5.3-6.6) and 6.4 (5.2-8.0) Gyr at M7 and M8. Both bins contain mostly stars, so these lifetimes describe the lowest-mass stars.

papers.title: A new angle on coherence-violating logarithms in color-singlet processes
papers.abstract: We introduce a new formulation for the resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the transverse energy flow in rapidity gaps in the Drell-Yan process. Our formalism allows us to resum coherence-violating logarithms in the gap cross section in the phenomenologically important regime where the gap size is comparable to the logarithm of the transverse energy. In the formal small gap limit, our result reduces to the known state-of-the-art resummation of coherence-violating logarithms for the Drell-Yan process. However, we identify sizable new corrections even for moderate gap widths that significantly modify the phenomenological picture for LHC applications. This work will form an important element of future extensions to a range of global and non-global observables.

papers.title: Statistical Properties of the $q$-Deformed Monolayer and Bilayer Graphene
papers.abstract: We investigate the statistical properties of the $q$-deformed Dirac oscillator for monolayer and bilayer graphene in the presence of a constant external magnetic field. Using $q$-deformed creation and annihilation operators, we obtain the corresponding energy spectra and eigenfunctions, as well as their probability current densities, recovering the conventional Landau-level structures in the undeformed limit. For bilayer graphene, the lowest Landau levels are explicitly constructed within the $q$-deformed framework. The partition functions for both systems are derived using zeta-function techniques and the Euler-Maclaurin formula, allowing us to determine their main thermodynamic quantities for small values of the deformation parameter. Our results show that the $q$-deformation modifies the energy spectra, the behavior of the probability current density components, and the thermodynamic response of the systems. A comparison between monolayer and bilayer graphene reveals distinct thermal behaviors, reflecting their different Landau-level structures and highlighting the influence of the $q$-deformation on their statistical properties.

papers.title: Observational diagnostics of external photoevaporation at millimetre wavelengths
papers.abstract: External photoevaporation is increasingly recognised as an important influence on protoplanetary disk evolution. However, there are no established molecular line diagnostics that can reliably distinguish external irradiation from variations in intrinsic stellar and disk properties. We use a large grid of thermochemical models to predict the fluxes of 48 transitions from eight species observable with ALMA, spanning a wide range of system properties and external FUV fields of 100 to 100,000 G0. At fixed stellar and disk properties, all transitions generally brighten with increasing FUV field strength. HCO+ and CO fluxes increase monotonically in virtually all disks, whereas lower-excitation lines, particularly those of C2H and N2H+, respond weakly and non-monotonically. However, variations in stellar mass and disk size introduce substantial degeneracies, limiting the usefulness of individual line fluxes as tracers of external irradiation. We therefore assess all pairwise line flux ratios, which can significantly reduce these degeneracies, evaluating their correlation with the external field, the magnitude of their change across the FUV range, and predicted ALMA detectability. We identify 135 promising ratios, including several combining strong FUV sensitivity and high detectability with efficient single-tuning ALMA observations. The strongest diagnostics either contrast high- and low-excitation lines of the same or co-spatial species (e.g. CO J=8-7/J=1-0), probing different regions of the photoevaporative wind, or pair an FUV-sensitive wind tracer with comparatively insensitive emission arising closer to the disk (e.g. HCO+ J=3-2/C2H N=3-2). Our results provide a framework for identifying externally photoevaporating systems from spatially unresolved emission and constraining their incident FUV field strengths.

papers.title: Absolute luminosity calibration of the LHCb detector in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with beam-gas imaging
authors: U. De Freitas Carneiro Da Graca
papers.abstract: An absolute calibration of the luminosity for proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV with the LHCb detector in Run 2 of the LHC is presented. papers.title: The phase gradient spectrum: probing the squeezed bispectrum of the 21-cm signal during reionization
papers.abstract: The 21-cm signal from the epoch of reionization is highly non-Gaussian. Standard analyses rely on the power spectrum, which is blind to the Fourier phases, while higher-order statistics such as the bispectrum are computationally expensive and spread information across triangle configurations. As an efficient alternative, we develop the \textit{phase gradient spectrum}, which measures the circular coherence of phase differences between Fourier modes separated by a long-wavelength mode. We show analytically that this statistic measures the angle-averaged normalised squeezed bispectrum, which describes the response of small-scale power to long-wavelength fluctuations. Applied to reionization simulations with different ionizing source properties, the phase gradient spectrum of the 21-cm signal shows a characteristic non-monotonic evolution. At early times, the spectrum tracks the non-Gaussianity of the matter density field. Once the mean neutral fraction $\langle x_\mathrm{HI}\rangle \lesssim 0.9$, the spectrum follows the ionization topology. The phase coherence reaches a minimum midway through reionization and rises again as the remaining neutral regions shrink into isolated islands. Statistics that keep the sign of the squeezed bispectrum show that this minimum marks its sign change. This evolution holds for different reionization models and simulation frameworks. A Fisher forecast for a 1000-h Square Kilometre Array (SKA)-Low observation, combining five redshifts across reionization, shows that the phase gradient spectrum alone constrains the astrophysical parameters, and these constraints tighten by a factor of $\gtrsim 2$ for a 10,000-h observation. Combining the phase gradient spectrum with the power spectrum tightens the marginalised constraints by up to $\sim$20 per cent relative to the power spectrum alone.

papers.title: Complete Cosmological Collider Signatures from Right-handed Neutrino Loops
papers.abstract: We study the complete cosmological collider (CC) signatures from right-handed neutrino loops with chemical-potential enhancement. These CC signals are induced by the inflaton-right-handed-neutrino interaction and can be extracted in the collinear squeezed configuration, which allows the right-handed-neutrino triangle loop to be factorized into the hard and soft parts. We precisely compute the soft part of the fermion loop for the first time by using the complete mode functions and the full loop integral, and treat the hard part as a tree-level subdiagram. We subtract the large-momentum asymptotic terms of the soft loop integrand and retain their finite contributions to the oscillation. We then evaluate the full spinor-helicity and Schwinger-Keldysh sums to obtain a finite, closed analytic formula for the complex clock coefficient. We further derive a compact formula for the leading CC signals in the large-chemical-potential expansion. We analyze the structure of the soft-part contribution by examining the sum of residues of the Mellin poles of the fermion propagators. For this, we demonstrate that the first local pole on each soft line contributes half of the asymptotic coefficient on one Schwinger-Keldysh path and the remaining local poles on the second soft line supply the other half.

papers.title: Nuclear mass calculation based on anisotropic kernel ridge regression and $α$-decay chain recursion
papers.abstract: Many short-lived or rarely produced nuclei defy direct mass spectrometry, but their masses are constrained by the $α$-decay energies connecting them through decay chains. We combine anisotropic kernel ridge regression (AKRR), an extended Garvey--Kelson relation (GK16), and $α$-decay chain recursion: AKRR learns the residuals between experimental $α$-decay energies and WS4 predictions, GK16 removes residual local fluctuations, and the corrected energies convert a measured anchor mass into the target mass by exact recursion---replacing absolute-mass extrapolation with interpolation of relative decay energies plus exact algebra. The only data-adjusted quantities are the three kernel hyperparameters, fixed by leave-one-out cross validation. For the 22 nuclei whose masses were measured only after AME2003, the $Q_α$ RMSD falls from 169~keV (WS4) to 108~keV (AKRR) and 65~keV (AKRR+GK16), and the mass-excess RMSD reaches 86~keV, versus 348 and 211~keV for WS4 and AKRR. Mass excesses are further predicted for the 122 nuclei with measured $Q_α$ but no directly measured masses.

papers.title: Strangeness-to-entropy ratio across the QCD crossover
papers.abstract: We study the absolute open-strangeness density $n_{|S|}$ of strongly interacting matter at vanishing conserved-charge chemical potentials. Unlike the net-strangeness susceptibility $χ_2^S$, this quantity is not a derivative of the QCD partition function and requires a microscopic specification of the strangeness carriers. We use an equation of state that interpolates between an interacting hadron resonance gas and a quark-gluon plasma, with parameters fixed previously by lattice-QCD bulk thermodynamics. The ratio of $n_{|S|}$ to the entropy density $s$ follows the hadron-gas behavior below $T\simeq120$ MeV, rises above the ideal massless $2+1$-flavor limit of approximately $0.053$ across the crossover, and approaches this limit from above at high temperature. The same equation of state, minimally extended to finite $μ_S$, captures the temperature dependence of the lattice-QCD $χ_2^S$. For uncorrelated singly-strange Boltzmann particles, the strangeness fluctuation factor $F_S=χ_2^S/(n_{|S|}/T^3)$ equals unity. Within the constructed equation of state, it deviates from unity by less than $10\%$. This allows us to estimate $n_{|S|}/s$ from lattice-QCD data on $χ_2^S$ and $s$. The lattice-based estimate reaches a maximum of $n_{|S|}/s\simeq0.063$ at $T\simeq220$ MeV, followed by a $20\%$ decrease towards the high-temperature limit.

papers.title: Imprints of Non-local Top-Higgs Interaction on Loop Induced Higgs Processes
papers.abstract: A composite Higgs arising from an underlying strong sector generally has non-local interactions with the elementary sector, formulated in terms of momentum-dependent form factors. We construct the minimal Ball-Chiu-type vertices consistent with gauge-invariant non-local $\bar{t}th$ couplings containing Wilson lines, where recursive Ward-Takahashi identities connect the Yukawa interaction to higher-order contact interactions. For a symmetric monopole form factor motivated by lowest-resonance dominance, we compute the top-loop contributions to $gg \to h$ and $h \to γγ$ amplitudes in closed form, and demonstrate a logarithmically enhanced deviation from the Standard Model. Current measurements at the LHC exclude the characteristic new physics scale below 3.6 TeV at $2σ$, while future colliders could extend the sensitivity to approximately 8 TeV.

papers.title: Cosmic Censorship in the Landscape of SUSY-Broken AdS Vacua
papers.abstract: We investigate signatures of weak cosmic censorship in non-supersymmetric vacua of both IIA and IIB string theory. In particular, we examine the Penrose Inequality, which can be proven holographically using Ryu-Takayanagi, and can be independently proven in SUSY AdS vacua for spherically symmetric initial data. We prove that any EFT of scalars coupled to gravity in AdS, including in particular those of string compactifications, satisfies both the Penrose Inequality and a positive mass theorem if a function that we call a "weak fake superpotential" exists. We demonstrate that this condition is satisfied globally for the DGKT skew-whiffed vacua in IIA. Since there is no known nonperturbative instability in this DGKT vacuum, this provides evidence that the IIA SUSY-broken AdS vacua may be absolutely stable. We also find the weak fake superpotential exists locally in field space in some SUSY-broken AdS vacua in a KKLT construction in IIB. Thus, within the framework considered here, some false SUSY-broken KKLT AdS vacua are stable against vacuum decay. Conversely, we find that some KKLT vacua do not have a weak fake superpotential, and correspondingly violate the Penrose Inequality and fail to have a positive mass theorem; the DGKT vacua only violate the Penrose Inequality in the presence of designer gravity boundary conditions. In all cases studied, this is due to false vacuum decay. We discuss the implications of these violations for holography and black hole thermodynamics in these SUSY-broken AdS vacua.

papers.title: Micro-Macro Tensor Neural Surrogates for Uncertainty Quantification in Collisional Plasma
papers.abstract: Plasma kinetic equations exhibit pronounced sensitivity to microscopic perturbations in model parameters and data, making reliable and efficient uncertainty quantification (UQ) essential for predictive simulations. However, the cost of uncertainty sampling, the high-dimensional phase space, and multiscale stiffness pose severe challenges to both computational efficiency and error control in traditional numerical methods. These aspects are further emphasized in presence of collisions where the high-dimensional nonlocal collision integrations and conservation properties pose severe constraints. To overcome this, we present a variance-reduced Monte Carlo framework for UQ in the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau (VPL) system, in which neural network surrogates replace the multiple costly evaluations of the Landau collision term. The method couples a high-fidelity, asymptotic-preserving VPL solver with inexpensive, strongly correlated surrogates based on the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Euler--Poisson (EP) equations. For the surrogate models, we introduce a generalization of the separable physics-informed neural network (SPINN), developing a class of tensor neural networks based on an anisotropic micro-macro decomposition, to reduce velocity-moment costs, model complexity, and the curse of dimensionality. To further increase correlation with VPL, we calibrate the VPFP model and design an asymptotic-preserving SPINN whose small- and large-Knudsen limits recover the EP and VP systems, respectively. Numerical experiments show substantial variance reduction over standard Monte Carlo, accurate statistics with far fewer high-fidelity samples, and lower wall-clock time, while maintaining robustness to stochastic dimension.
